clue.text: Sermon where one regularly sleeps?

definitions.meaning: a speech delivered formally to an audience, as a preacher gives from the pulpit
the place you live, given as street and number on letters

explanation.surface: A dull sermon is the place where the congregation habitually nods off.
explanation.definitionFit: A sermon is a formal speech, and the second sense is the home location written on an envelope.

clue.text: Sedative may wander and lose the point … lose the point …

indicators.note: may wander says the letters of the word sedative drift into a new order
lose says a compass point is taken out

parts.note: S is south, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A drowsy patient on a sedative drifts off topic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lose' drops S (south, a point of the compass) from SEDATIVE, and 'may wander' rearranges what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: To depart from the subject, losing the point, is to stray or digress.

clue.text: River in Kent occurs in the Wash?

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river on maps
taken as written
Kent is a county in South East England, abbreviated SE

explanation.surface: A river in Kent flows into the Wash, the bay on the east coast.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wash is a large bay on England's east coast; here it is just a wash. Kent, a county in South East England, gives SE.
explanation.definitionFit: To rinse something is to wash it lightly in clean water.

clue.text: Tawdry stuff in certain eminence

indicators.note: in says the tawdry stuff goes inside the word for certain

parts.note: certain means sure
tat is cheap, tasteless goods

explanation.surface: Cheap goods found in the home of a certain grandee.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing or reputation, as in a person of eminence, is a figurative synonym.

clue.text: It's this or nothing at breakfast, say

definitions.text: It's this or nothing at breakfast, say

parts.note: nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O
taken as written
breakfast is an example of a meal

explanation.surface: A diner insists that porridge oats are the only acceptable morning food.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground oats boiled into porridge are a classic breakfast dish, so the whole clue describes the food.

clue.text: For each one baked item is included

indicators.note: is included says the baked item goes inside the word for one

parts.note: an ace is a one in a pack of cards
a pie is something baked

explanation.surface: Each guest gets a baked dish included in the price.
explanation.definitionFit: Each, apiece and per head all mean distributed one to every person.

clue.text: Sales require boy to get in difficulty

parts.note: Mark is a boy's name

indicators.note: difficulty suggests the words are in trouble and so get jumbled

explanation.surface: A lad has to try hard to break into a tough line of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in difficulty' looks like the whole anagram signal, but 'in' is fodder, so 'difficulty' alone stirs GET IN; Mark is the boy.
explanation.definitionFit: The business of selling and promoting goods covers the sales side.

clue.text: Mechanic has no end of sanitary work

indicators.note: work says the remaining letters are worked into a new order
no end of says the word sanitary loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A plumber is busy on endless sanitary jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end of' trims sanitary to SANITAR, and 'work' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled manual worker; mechanic is an old word for a craftsman or artisan.

clue.text: Olden times where memories are fading?

parts.note: olden means older, so senior
moments are short periods of time

explanation.surface: Nostalgia for the good old days when people misremember.
explanation.definitionFit: Brief lapses of memory blamed on age are where recollection fades.

clue.text: Time that's endless, never over

indicators.note: over means the trimmed letters are turned backwards
endless means the word never loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone muses that time without end never finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims never to NEVE, and 'over' turns NEVE round.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic word for evening, the time of day at the close of daylight.

clue.text: Meal — tea or one possibly better …

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of these words might be rearranged into something else

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a meal or just tea would be the better choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges MEAL, TEA, OR and I (one) into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To improve a situation, making it better, is a formal verb synonym.

clue.text: … state meal with posh cake

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
tea is an afternoon or evening meal in Britain
U means upper-class, as in the old U and non-U distinction

explanation.surface: An official state banquet ends with a fancy dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich, elaborate cream cake, from the French word for cake.

clue.text: Lest surrounded, soldiers proliferate

indicators.note: surrounded says the soldiers are placed inside the phrase meaning lest

parts.note: lest means in case, two words run together
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Troops multiply for fear of being encircled.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow in number or spread rapidly is to multiply, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Nice 1 for some locals

parts.note: 1 across refers to a form of address; in the French city of Nice, men are addressed with the plural French title

explanation.surface: A pleasant chat-up opening for the residents of some place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, not the adjective, and 1 is the entry at 1 across, ADDRESS: the French plural form of address for men.
explanation.definitionFit: The French plural of the title Monsieur, used when addressing gentlemen in Nice.

clue.text: Superiority is in 4, declares sex expert

indicators.note: declares says the phrase is spoken and the sound is what is entered

parts.note: 4 down is a word for stature, and superiority in stature is sheer height

explanation.surface: A sexologist claims superiority lies in a person's stature.
explanation.walkthrough: Shere Hite was an American sex researcher, author of the Hite Report; 4 refers to 4 down, STATURE.
explanation.definitionFit: An American sexologist famous for the Hite Report on female sexuality.

clue.text: Close acquaintance not right with the devil

indicators.note: not says the abbreviation for right is left out of the word for a close acquaintance

parts.note: a close acquaintance is a friend

explanation.surface: A close companion is not in the right if keeping company with Satan.
explanation.definitionFit: A demon or evil spirit is a devil, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Day's march for a Roman soldier?

definitions.meaning: a distance marched in a day would be measured in units of length like this
Latin for a soldier, the common foot soldier of the Roman army

explanation.surface: How far a legionary could tramp in one day.
explanation.definitionFit: Units of distance cover a day's march, and the Latin word for a soldier is spelt the same.

clue.text: Step of 14 into wrecked semi, from which there's no way out

definitions.text: from which there's no way out

indicators.note: into says the step goes inside the rearranged letters
wrecked says the letters of the word semi are smashed into a new order

parts.note: 14 across is French plural address, and pas is French for a step

explanation.surface: A dance step taken into a ruined semi-detached house leads to a dead end.
explanation.walkthrough: The 14 points to the French plural address, so the step is French; 'wrecked' scrambles semi to IMSE and 'into' places the step inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock or dead end is a situation with no way out.

clue.text: It's pitiful, for instance, in new oboe composition

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation for instance goes inside the rearranged letters
composition says the letters of the two words are put together in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
EG is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for instance

explanation.surface: A new piece of music for oboe sounds sad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' is a link before the definition; 'composition' gives WOEBONE from the two words, and 'in' puts the instance abbreviation inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking sad and miserable, so pitiful in appearance, is a synonym.

clue.text: It's some way off a bull — almost

definitions.text: It's some way off a bull — almost

indicators.note: some way says the letters are arranged in some other way
almost says the word bull loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A creature that is nearly, but not quite, a bull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims bull to BUL, and 'some way' rearranges OFFA plus BUL.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild ox, close to but not quite cattle, and also a city some way off.

clue.text: Fabric from Granny Sharp?

parts.note: nan is a familiar word for a grandmother
keen means sharp, as of a blade

explanation.surface: A cloth supplied by a grandmother called Sharp.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellowish cotton cloth originally from Nanjing, a type of fabric.

clue.text: Very hot, like the boy in title's opening letter?

parts.note: Pip is the boy hero of Great Expectations
taken as written
the title Great Expectations begins with the letter G

explanation.surface: A scorching question about a boy at the start of a book title.
explanation.walkthrough: Pip is the hero of Dickens's Great Expectations, whose title opens with G.
explanation.definitionFit: Piping hot is an idiom for food that is very hot.

clue.text: Primate retains little desire for nourishment

indicators.note: retains says the primate holds the word for little within it

parts.note: an ape is a primate
petit is French for little, also used in English as in petit four

explanation.surface: A monkey keeps a small craving for food.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunger, a wish to eat, is a desire for nourishment.

clue.text: What's left in remains of a gender issue

indicators.note: in says the answer is buried inside the run of clue words

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what is left in the debris of a gender debate.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is held in 'of a gender'; 'remains' and 'issue' are surface dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: The stub of a cigarette, and by extension any useless leftover remnant.

clue.text: Sound of sporty car getting run in?

indicators.note: in says the run goes inside the sporty car abbreviation

parts.note: GT is a gran turismo, a sports car
taken as written

explanation.surface: The noise a sports car makes on a run.
explanation.definitionFit: A short guttural noise, like a pig's, is a kind of sound.

clue.text: Part is said to develop from an old house plant

indicators.note: to develop says the letters of the three words grow into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardening tip about a cutting grown from an old pot plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to develop' rearranges PART, IS and SAID into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough, leafy pot plant beloved of Victorian parlours, a type of houseplant.

clue.text: Wearer of trousers, sort about to be dropped?

indicators.note: to be dropped says these letters fall out of the word trousers

parts.note: taken as written; the setter removes scattered letters, so the run left inside this word is a coincidence, not a hidden word

indicators.note: about says the word sort is read backwards

explanation.surface: Asks what kind of person wears trousers, about to drop them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns sort into TROS, and 'to be dropped' takes T, R, O and S out of TROUSERS.
explanation.definitionFit: One who wears or uses something, so a wearer is a person making use of it.

clue.text: Should tax system turn out for good, result could be sweet

indicators.note: out for says one letter leaves and the other takes its place

parts.note: the revenue is the government department collecting taxes
U stands for turn, as in a U-turn

explanation.surface: If the taxman changed things for the better, the outcome would please.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' is U (a U-turn), swapped 'out for' G (good) in REVENUE.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says this retaliation is sweet, so a sweet result describes it.

clue.text: Betoken the last of the wine

indicators.note: of says the final part belongs to the wine, so it follows it

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
the last of something is its end

explanation.surface: The final drop of wine is an omen.
explanation.definitionFit: To foreshadow or signify in advance is a synonym for betoken.
